statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Every one of the 24 published hours falls inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form within the window, while the macro backdrop behind elevated Stress remains unresolved.

headline: Nasdaq-100 inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail at its floor with Stress elevated on 5.165% long-end yields, $92 crude and unresolved Hormuz diplomacy
body: Friday's session closed in orderly, two-sided fashion. Cash NDX finished 30,608.14, up 0.42% or 129.28 points, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 0.19% below the session high, while NQ Dec-26 was last 30,921.75, up 0.50%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range and about 0.24% below its high. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range. All three major US averages posted weekly gains, with the Dow up 0.93% to 51,828.62 and snapping a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 up 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not pin to an extreme, so there is no evidence of persistent one-way structure or repeated extension after failed pullbacks. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, beyond the final published hour; the NAS100 CFD follows the same closure. Because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, Tail is held at its floor for every hour of the window. The environment behind Stress nonetheless remains genuinely difficult. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.165% after easing about 4 basis points on Friday from multi-decade highs, with the H.15 release showing 2-year 4.87%, 10-year 5.18% and 30-year 5.47% for September 24, and roughly a 66% implied probability of a further 25 basis point Fed increase at the next meeting. Cleveland Fed President Hammack attributed elevated long-end yields to the growth outlook, federal debt and the expected rate path. WTI is $92.44, down 2.29% on Friday and about 7.4% on the week but still roughly 12.4% higher over the month, with Brent below $98; the Strait of Hormuz has been closed since 28 February 2026. Iran's foreign minister proposed reopening the strait within seven days, with preparatory steps over four to five days, an opening on day six and nuclear talks on day seven, conditional on the US lifting its naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and observing a ceasefire including Lebanon. The proposal was conveyed through Qatar; the White House described conversations with mediators as positive and constructive without commenting on the terms, and no acceptance is verified. Attacks on commercial shipping in the strait have continued through September. Final September Michigan sentiment printed 48.1, a four-month low, with 1-year inflation expectations at 4.6%, and the Trump-Xi state visit closed with few concrete trade outcomes. Friday internals were uneven rather than aligned: the Russell 2000 added only 0.07% against the Dow's 0.93%, and megacap dispersion reached 1.92 percentage points with MSFT up 3.66% and AAPL up 1.53% against META down 3.33% and TSLA down 1.54%. Semiconductors were mostly higher, led by QCOM up 3.97% and ARM up 1.30%, with INTC down 3.45%. Under the contract, conflicting internals and unresolved policy overhangs inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. Shared Finviz context was 95 minutes old at assessment and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale corroboration only; its delayed latest-session breadth, showing Technology up 0.85% and semiconductors up 0.56%, agreed with independently verified closing data and changed no conclusion. Stress is therefore held inside the elevated band throughout, easing to 45 through the quiet Saturday hours and firming back to 50 by the end of the window as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates ahead of the reopen. Confidence starts at 85 on a complete set of verified closing levels, official yields, energy prices, volatility readings and calendar detail, and decays across the window purely as Friday's last verified observation ages.
